# netbox_available_prefix (Resource)

A NetBox prefix (ipam.prefix) allocated as the next free child prefix of the given length inside a parent prefix. After creation it is an ordinary prefix; the allocation inputs replace the resource when changed. Import with "parent_prefix_id/prefix_id/prefix_length".

From the [official documentation](https://netboxlabs.com/docs/netbox/models/ipam/prefix/):

> A prefix is an IPv4 or IPv6 network and mask expressed in CIDR notation (e.g. 192.0.2.0/24). A prefix entails only the "network portion" of an IP address: All bits in the address not covered by the mask must be zero. (In other words, a prefix cannot be a specific IP address.) Prefixes are automatically organized by their parent [aggregate](https://netboxlabs.com/docs/netbox/models/ipam/aggregate/) and assigned [VRF](https://netboxlabs.com/docs/netbox/models/ipam/vrf/).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "netbox_prefix" "test" {
  prefix = "192.0.2.0/24"
  status = "container"
}

resource "netbox_tenant" "test" {
  name = "test-tenant"
}

# Allocates the next free /26 inside the parent prefix.
resource "netbox_available_prefix" "test" {
  parent_prefix_id = netbox_prefix.test.id
  prefix_length    = 26
  status           = "active"
  tenant_id        = netbox_tenant.test.id
  description      = "test-description"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `parent_prefix_id` (Number) Id of the prefix to allocate the child prefix from.
- `prefix_length` (Number) Length of the prefix to allocate (0-128).

### Optional

- `comments` (String)
- `custom_fields` (Map of String) Custom field values by field name. Every value is a string; NetBox coerces numbers and booleans. A key removed from the map is cleared in NetBox (set {} to clear all).
- `description` (String)
- `is_pool` (Boolean) All addresses within this prefix are usable.
- `location_id` (Number) Id of the location the object is scoped to (scope_type dcim.location).
- `mark_utilized` (Boolean) Report space as fully utilized.
- `owner_id` (Number) Id of the owner the object is assigned to.
- `region_id` (Number) Id of the region the object is scoped to (scope_type dcim.region).
- `role_id` (Number) Id of the role.
- `scope_id` (Number) Id of the scope object (see scope_type).
- `scope_type` (String) Content type of the scope. Derived from site_id, location_id, region_id or site_group_id when one of those is set; set it together with scope_id otherwise. One of: dcim.site, dcim.location, dcim.region, dcim.sitegroup.
- `site_group_id` (Number) Id of the site group the object is scoped to (scope_type dcim.sitegroup).
- `site_id` (Number) Id of the site the object is scoped to (scope_type dcim.site). Conflicts with the other scope aliases and with setting the scope_* pair directly.
- `status` (String) Operational status. One of: container, active, reserved, deprecated.
- `tags` (Set of String) Slugs of the tags assigned to the object (the provider's default_tags are added on top, see tags_all).
- `tenant_id` (Number) Id of the tenant.
- `vlan_id` (Number) Id of the VLAN.
- `vrf_id` (Number) Id of the VRF.

### Read-Only

- `created` (String)
- `id` (Number) NetBox id.
- `last_updated` (String)
- `prefix` (String) The allocated IPv4 or IPv6 network with mask, e.g. 10.0.1.0/24.
- `tags_all` (Set of String) Slugs of all tags on the object, including the provider's default_tags.
- `url` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# parent_prefix_id/prefix_id/prefix_length
import {
  to = netbox_available_prefix.test
  id = "1/2/24"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# parent_prefix_id/prefix_id/prefix_length
terraform import netbox_available_prefix.test 1/2/24
```
